contentObjective: I can estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents, rounding, and compatible numbers.
languageObjective: I can explain an estimate using the words about, benchmark, and compatible numbers.

vocabulary.definition: A reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful, found without exact computation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta razonada, lo bastante cercana para ser útil, sin cálculo exacto.
vocabulary.example: 8.6% of 216 is about 10% of 220, which is 22.
vocabulary.cloze: A reasoned answer close enough to be useful is an ___.

examples.text: “About 20 pounds” when the exact answer is 18.576
examples.why: Close enough to plan with, found without exact computation.
That is the exact answer, not an estimate.

vocabulary.definition: A friendly percent — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — used as a landmark for estimating.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje amigable — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — que sirve de punto de referencia.
vocabulary.example: 4 GB of 6 GB sits between the 50% and 75% marks.
vocabulary.visual: 1% · 10% · 25% · 50% · 75% · 100% — the landmarks you can find mentally.
vocabulary.cloze: A friendly percent used as a landmark, like 10% or 25%, is a ___ ___.

examples.text: Using 50% because half of an amount is easy
examples.why: It is one of the percents you can find in your head.

examples.text: Using 37% because it is in the problem
examples.why: It is exact, but nothing about it is mentally friendly.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers close to the originals that are easy to compute with mentally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números cercanos a los originales con los que es fácil calcular mentalmente.
vocabulary.visual: 8.6% of 216 → 10% of 220: both nudged to numbers that divide nicely.
vocabulary.cloze: Numbers close to the originals that are easy to compute with are ___ ___.

examples.why: 200 is close by and 10% of it is instant.
It is easy to compute, but far too far from the original.

vocabulary.definition: Two parallel number lines that pair amounts with their percents at the same positions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas paralelas que emparejan cantidades con sus porcentajes en las mismas posiciones.
vocabulary.example: GB on top, percent on the bottom: 1.5 GB lines up with 25%.
vocabulary.cloze: Two parallel lines pairing amounts with their percents form a ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Dollars marked on one line and percents on the other, lined up
examples.why: Matching positions pair an amount with its percent.

examples.text: One number line with only percents on it
examples.why: With nothing to pair against, there is no second quantity.

vocabulary.definition: The quantity that counts as 100% in a problem — and it can change between questions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que representa el 100% en un problema, y puede cambiar entre preguntas.
vocabulary.example: First the whole is 6 GB; for the photos question the whole becomes the 4 GB used.
vocabulary.visual: “Of the USED storage” makes 4 GB the whole — not the 6 GB total.
vocabulary.cloze: The quantity that counts as 100% in a problem is ___ ___.

examples.text: The 60 students in the class when 18 of them walk
examples.why: It is the amount the percent is measured against.
That is the part; the percent describes it, it is not the whole.

vocabulary.definition: Break a percent into friendly pieces that are easy to find.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un porcentaje en partes fáciles de calcular.
vocabulary.cloze: Breaking 15% into 10% plus 5% is called ___ the percent.

examples.why: The percent is split into easy pieces.
That uses the whole percent at once.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Food Drive
revealWordProblem.text:
The organizers of a food drive set a new goal for a second food drive. They hope to collect 140% as many cans as they did last time, when they collected 145 cans.
Question: About how many cans can the organizers expect to collect? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Estimate with benchmark percents. 145 rounds to 150, and 140% is 100% + 40%. 100% of 150 is 150, and 40% of 150 is 60, so 150 + 60 = 210 cans — about 200. Checking exactly: 1.4 × 145 = 203, which is close to the estimate, so about 200 cans is a reasonable expectation.

questions.stem: Margaret's phone has 6 GB of storage and 4 GB is used. About what percent is used?
questions.explanation: 4 out of 6 is 2/3, which is about 67%, so 'about 70%' is the reasonable estimate.
choiceFeedback: 25% of 6 GB would be only 1.5 GB.
That reads the 4 GB as 40% — but the whole is 6, not 10.
More than 100% would mean using more storage than the phone has.
hints: What is the whole?
4 out of 6 is the same as 2 out of 3.
Two-thirds is close to which benchmark?
questions.stemEs: El teléfono de Margaret tiene 6 GB de almacenamiento y 4 GB están usados. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje está usado?
questions.explanationEs: 4 de 6 es 2/3, que es aproximadamente 67%, así que 'aproximadamente 70%' es la estimación razonable.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el entero?
4 de 6 es lo mismo que 2 de 3.
¿Dos tercios está cerca de cuál punto de referencia?

questions.stem: On the double number line for 6 GB, what amount lines up with 25%?
questions.explanation: 25% of 6 GB is one quarter of 6, which is 1.5 GB.
choiceFeedback: That divides 6 by 4.8 rather than by 4.
2.5 GB would be more than a third of the storage.
hints: 25% means one quarter.
One quarter of 6.
questions.stemEs: En la recta numérica doble para 6 GB, ¿qué cantidad se alinea con 25%?
questions.explanationEs: 25% de 6 GB es una cuarta parte de 6, que es 1.5 GB.
hintsEs: 25% significa una cuarta parte.
Una cuarta parte de 6.

questions.stem: Which benchmark percents make good landmarks on a number line?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 25 (and 10) are friendly landmarks because their amounts are easy to compute.
choiceFeedback: Those percents are no easier to compute with than the original problem.
50% alone leaves most of the line unmarked.
100% alone gives you nothing to compare against in the middle.
hints: Which percents can you find mentally?
Quarters and tenths are the friendly ones.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuáles porcentajes de referencia sirven bien como puntos guía en una recta numérica?
questions.explanationEs: Los múltiplos de 25 (y de 10) son puntos de referencia amigables porque sus cantidades son fáciles de calcular.
hintsEs: ¿Cuáles porcentajes puedes hallar mentalmente?
Los cuartos y los décimos son los amigables.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: Keeping the same whole for every question — when the problem says 'of the used storage,' the whole changes from 6 GB to 4 GB, and estimates anchored to the old whole are wrong before any arithmetic happens.

hints: 10.2% is about 10%. 798 is about 800.
hintsEs: El 10.2% es aproximadamente 10%. 798 es aproximadamente 800.
level1.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 10.2% → 10%; 798 → 800 Find the scale factor from 100 to 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide the whole by 10 too: 800 ÷ 10 = 80
level1.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 10.2% → 10%; 798 → 800 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide el entero entre 10 también: 800 ÷ 10 = 80

hints: 24% is about 25%, which is one quarter. 119 is about 120.
hintsEs: El 24% es aproximadamente 25%, que es una cuarta parte. 119 es aproximadamente 120.
level1.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 24% → 25%; 119 → 120 Find the scale factor from 100 to 25: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 Divide the whole by 4 too: 120 ÷ 4 = 30
level1.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 24% → 25%; 119 → 120 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 25: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 Divide el entero entre 4 también: 120 ÷ 4 = 30

hints: 48% is about 50%. Find half of a friendly number near 142.
hintsEs: El 48% es aproximadamente 50%. Halla la mitad de un número amigable cerca de 142.
level1.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 48% → 50%; 142 → 140 Find the scale factor from 100 to 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide the whole by 2 too: 140 ÷ 2 = 70
level1.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 48% → 50%; 142 → 140 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide el entero entre 2 también: 140 ÷ 2 = 70

hints: 49% is close to 50%. Find half of a friendly number near 82.
hintsEs: El 49% está cerca del 50%. Halla la mitad de un número amigable cerca de 82.
level1.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 49% → 50%; 82 → 80 Find the scale factor from 100 to 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide the whole by 2 too: 80 ÷ 2 = 40
level1.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 49% → 50%; 82 → 80 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide el entero entre 2 también: 80 ÷ 2 = 40

hints: Round 10.4% to 10%. Round 587 to a friendly number. Then move the decimal point.
hintsEs: Redondea 10.4% a 10%. Redondea 587 a un número amigable. Luego mueve el punto decimal.
level1.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 10.4% → 10%; 587 → 600 Find the scale factor from 100 to 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide the whole by 10 too: 600 ÷ 10 = 60
level1.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 10.4% → 10%; 587 → 600 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide el entero entre 10 también: 600 ÷ 10 = 60

level2.stem: Jay estimates 52% of 198 as about 200. Is his estimate reasonable?
level2.stemEs: Jay estima el 52% de 198 como aproximadamente 200. ¿Es razonable su estimación?
hints: 52% is close to which benchmark? What is that benchmark of 200?
hintsEs: ¿El 52% está cerca de qué referencia? ¿Cuánto es esa referencia de 200?
level2.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 52% → 50%; 198 → 200 Find the scale factor from 100 to 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide the whole by 2 too: 200 ÷ 2 = 100
level2.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 52% → 50%; 198 → 200 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide el entero entre 2 también: 200 ÷ 2 = 100
choices: No. 52% is about half, so it is about 100.
choicesEs: No. El 52% es como la mitad, así que es aproximadamente 100.
choiceFeedback: Jay rounded the number but forgot the percent. 200 is all of it, or 100%.
52 is the percent, not the part. Use 50% of 200.

level2.stemEs: Estima el 61% de 497. Combina porcentajes de referencia.
hints: Round to 60% and 500. Find 10% first, then multiply by 6.
hintsEs: Redondea a 60% y 500. Halla primero el 10%, luego multiplica por 6.
level2.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 61% → 60%; 497 → 500 Divide both by 10 to find 10%: 500 ÷ 10 = 50 Multiply both by 6 to find 60%: 50 × 6 = 300
level2.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 61% → 60%; 497 → 500 Divide los dos entre 10 para hallar el 10%: 500 ÷ 10 = 50 Multiplica los dos por 6 para hallar el 60%: 50 × 6 = 300

hints: Round 10.7% to 10%. Round 893 to a friendly number.
hintsEs: Redondea 10.7% a 10%. Redondea 893 a un número amigable.
level2.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 10.7% → 10%; 893 → 900 Find the scale factor from 100 to 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide the whole by 10 too: 900 ÷ 10 = 90
level2.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 10.7% → 10%; 893 → 900 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide el entero entre 10 también: 900 ÷ 10 = 90

level2.stem: Estimate 11% of 516 with benchmarks. Is your estimate a little high or a little low?
level2.stemEs: Estima el 11% de 516 con referencias. ¿Tu estimación es un poco alta o un poco baja?
hints: Round 11% to 10% and 516 to 500. Then think about which way you rounded.
hintsEs: Redondea 11% a 10% y 516 a 500. Luego piensa hacia dónde redondeaste.
level2.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 11% → 10%; 516 → 500 Find the scale factor from 100 to 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide the whole by 10 too: 500 ÷ 10 = 50
level2.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 11% → 10%; 516 → 500 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Divide el entero entre 10 también: 500 ÷ 10 = 50

level2.stem: A bike costs $159. It is on sale for 24% off. About how much money do you save?
level2.stemEs: Una bicicleta cuesta $159. Está en oferta con 24% de descuento. ¿Aproximadamente cuánto dinero ahorras?
hints: 24% is close to 25%, which is one quarter. Round $159 to a number easy to divide by 4.
hintsEs: El 24% está cerca del 25%, que es una cuarta parte. Redondea $159 a un número fácil de dividir entre 4.
level2.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 24% → 25%; $159 → $160 Find the scale factor from 100 to 25: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 Divide the whole by 4 too: 160 ÷ 4 = 40
level2.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 24% → 25%; $159 → $160 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 25: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 Divide el entero entre 4 también: 160 ÷ 4 = 40

level3.stem: A jacket originally priced at $78.99 is on sale for 25% off. Which is the best estimate of the discount amount?
choiceFeedback: That is about 10% of $80. 25% is two and a half times that much.
That is about one eighth of $80. 25% is one QUARTER, so divide $80 by 4.
That is half of $80. 25% is half of 50%, so halve it once more.
level3.explanation: Round $78.99 to $80. 25% is 1/4 of the whole. 1/4 of $80 is $20.

level3.stem: Nia estimates 4.8% of 610. She says 10% of 600 is 60, so the answer is about 60. Find a better estimate.
level3.stemEs: Nia estima el 4.8% de 610. Dice que el 10% de 600 es 60, así que la respuesta es aproximadamente 60. Halla una mejor estimación.
hints: Which benchmark is closest to 4.8%? It is half of 10%.
hintsEs: ¿Qué referencia está más cerca de 4.8%? Es la mitad del 10%.
level3.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 4.8% → 5%; 610 → 600 Divide both by 10 to find 10%: 600 ÷ 10 = 60 Divide both by 2 to find 5%: 60 ÷ 2 = 30
level3.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 4.8% → 5%; 610 → 600 Divide los dos entre 10 para hallar el 10%: 600 ÷ 10 = 60 Divide los dos entre 2 para hallar el 5%: 60 ÷ 2 = 30

level3.stemEs: Estima el 73% de 812. Usa porcentajes de referencia.
hints: Round to 75% and 800. Find 25% first, then multiply by 3.
hintsEs: Redondea a 75% y 800. Halla primero el 25%, luego multiplica por 3.
level3.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 73% → 75%; 812 → 800 Divide both by 4 to find 25%: 800 ÷ 4 = 200 Multiply both by 3 to find 75%: 200 × 3 = 600
level3.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 73% → 75%; 812 → 800 Divide los dos entre 4 para hallar el 25%: 800 ÷ 4 = 200 Multiplica los dos por 3 para hallar el 75%: 200 × 3 = 600

level3.stem: A road trip is 386 miles long. You have driven 52% of the trip. About how many miles have you driven?
level3.stemEs: Un viaje por carretera mide 386 millas. Has manejado el 52% del viaje. ¿Aproximadamente cuántas millas has manejado?
hints: 52% is close to 50%. Round 386 to a number that is easy to halve.
hintsEs: El 52% está cerca del 50%. Redondea 386 a un número fácil de dividir a la mitad.
level3.explanation: Round to friendly numbers: 52% → 50%; 386 → 400 Find the scale factor from 100 to 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide the whole by 2 too: 400 ÷ 2 = 200
level3.explanationEs: Redondea a números compatibles: 52% → 50%; 386 → 400 Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 50: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Divide el entero entre 2 también: 400 ÷ 2 = 200

level3.stem: A tank holds 38 gallons. It has 9 gallons in it. Use compatible numbers to estimate what percent full the tank is.
level3.stemEs: Un tanque tiene capacidad para 38 galones. Tiene 9 galones. Usa números compatibles para estimar qué porcentaje del tanque está lleno.
hints: Change 38 to a nearby number that 9 divides evenly.
hintsEs: Cambia 38 por un número cercano que 9 divida exactamente.
level3.explanation: Change 38 to a compatible number: 38 → 36 Find the scale factor from 36 to 9: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 Divide 100% by 4 too: 100 ÷ 4 = 25
level3.explanationEs: Cambia 38 por un número compatible: 38 → 36 Halla el factor de escala de 36 a 9: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 Divide 100% entre 4 también: 100 ÷ 4 = 25
